newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian money market listless on reporting day.
newsitem.headline: Indian money market listless on reporting day.

text.p: Indian overnight money was quoted in the 0.25-0.5 percent range in mid-morning trade on Friday, the day banks report their positions to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), dealers said.
Banks do not normally borrow on reporting days as it increases their reserve requirements for the next fortnight.
Dealers said no deals had taken place in government bonds.
They said three-day money was traded in the 6.0-7.0 percent range on Friday, indicating that call money was likely to open above 10 percent on Saturday, the first day of the next reporting fortnight.

"We are not sure how call money will open tomorrow but it should be firm," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Besides the tax outflows, there is also a 20 billion rupee securities auction on Monday. Call money should be firm next week..around 10 percent."

Dealers said banks were feeling the effect of funds outflow on account of tax payments by corporates earlier this month. Analysts have estimated the tax payments to be between 40 and 50 billion rupeees.
